acceptance_criteria: One health request calls runtime.getHealthSnapshot exactly once in every runtime mode.
A runtime transition injected between dependency evaluation steps cannot create a mixed-generation response.
Top-level status, degradation causes, runtime data, turn capability, and enrichment runtime status bind to the same sample generation.
Enrichment backlog is queried once through #2514's typed observation contract, with failure distinct from measured zero.
A recovery transition produces either a complete earlier degraded generation or a complete later healthy generation, never a hybrid.
Observation start, end, duration, and serialization time have explicit semantics and clock-skew tests.
Concurrent request tests prove snapshots do not share mutable observation state across requests.
Runtime snapshot exceptions produce typed readiness-unavailable state while the public process-liveness endpoint remains answerable.
Mutation tests fail if a projection re-calls the runtime or re-queries an already-owned probe.
Exact-byte tests contain only reserved opaque observation identifiers and no identity, content, location, process, credential, or topology values.

falsifier_or_remaining_gap: The finding would be falsified if every request sampled runtime exactly once and all status and projection fields derived from that immutable value. Exact source execution instead produced runtime_calls=2 with first_sample_degraded=true and second_sample_healthy=true. Existing tests establish adapter and health behavior separately but do not inject a transition through the complete request, and this review did not add concurrent-request or mutation fixtures.
impact: One response can carry healthy serialized runtime state while retaining degradation from an earlier sample, or mix older enrichment fields with newer runtime state. Consumers cannot distinguish a real transition from an internally incoherent observation.
